cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Philippi, and he's just told them he counts everything as loss for the sake of knowing the One he calls his Lord (Philippians 1:1; 3:8). Now he stops to set the record straight: he hasn't already obtained all this, and he hasn't already been made perfect. Friend, if PAUL is still a work in progress, I can stop beating myself up over the blurry stamps that landed me in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul hasn't been made perfect yet. So what does he say he does?

answers.text: He presses on to take hold of it
He waits for it to come to him
He rests on what he has done

cards.text: Paul says it again: Brothers, he doesn't consider himself to have taken hold of it yet. But there's ONE thing he does, and it's all about moving forward.

cards.question: Part of the one thing Paul does is forgetting something. What does he say he's forgetting?

cards.text: So Paul forgets what's behind, strains toward what's ahead, and presses on toward the goal. I tried hopping forward while looking BACK over my shoulder once, friend, and me and the chocolate chips got real close, real fast.

cards.question: Paul presses on toward the goal to win the ___ of God's heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul widens it out beyond himself: "All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view."

cards.question: Paul says that if someone thinks differently about some issue, God will reveal this to them as well.
Some may still think differently. Nevertheless, what does Paul say we must do?

answers.text: Live up to what we have already attained
Keep quiet until everyone finally agrees
Stop and wait until more is revealed

cards.text: Now Paul points the Philippians to an example to follow, which is how anybody learns a new job, friend. Just don't shadow ME, the stamper who once stamped an oven mitt twelve times before noticing it wasn't dough.

cards.question: Paul tells the Philippians to join one another in following an example. Whose?
Besides following Paul's example, who does Paul tell the Philippians to carefully observe?

answers.text: Those who walk by the pattern he set
Those who lead the local synagogue
Those who are rich and well known

cards.text: Then Paul says something he's told them often before, and now he says it again, even with tears. I think this one hurts.

cards.question: Paul says many live as ___ of the cross of Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul describes them: "Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame."

cards.question: Paul says the enemies of the cross have their minds set on heavenly things.
The enemies of the cross have their minds set on earthly things. But where does Paul say our citizenship is?

cards.text: And from heaven, Paul says, we eagerly await a Savior. Not just wait, friend, EAGERLY await, like somebody with their nose on the front window every time a car slows down.

cards.question: Paul says we eagerly await a Savior from heaven. Who does he name?

cards.text: This Savior has the power to subject all things to Himself, and with it He will transform our lowly bodies. Friend, when an angel called me out of a junk drawer, my worn-out edges came out sharp and new, and I'm telling you, being made new is GOOD.

cards.question: Jesus will transform our lowly bodies to be like His ___ body.

cards.text: Then Paul wraps it all up with a "Therefore," and look how he talks to them: "my brothers, whom I love and long for…"

cards.question: Paul calls the Philippians his joy and crown.
Paul ends with a word to his beloved Philippians. What does he tell them they must do?
